task_spec.title: Simulation Task
task_spec.description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: Mask adoption propagates via social ties; each person's adoption probability is updated based on the fraction of their contacts who currently adopt and their susceptibility.

interactions.name: policy_compliance
interactions.description: Policies (mandates, messaging, incentives) modify individual adoption propensity according to policy sensitivity and enforcement.

interactions.name: location_enforcement
interactions.description: Locations enforce mask requirements, influencing observed compliance and adjusting perceived costs/benefits of adoption.

interactions.name: attendance_contacts
interactions.description: People attend locations, generating contacts that determine peer exposure and observed compliance signals.

metrics.name: RMSE
metrics.description: Root Mean Squared Error between simulated and observed daily mask adoption rates over the calibration period.

metrics.name: MAE
metrics.description: Mean Absolute Error between simulated and observed daily mask adoption rates.

metrics.name: FinalAdoptionRate
metrics.description: Simulated adoption proportion on the final day of the calibration period.

metrics.name: TimeToTargetAdoption
metrics.description: Number of days until simulated adoption first reaches or exceeds a specified target threshold.

metrics.name: PeakAdoptionDay
metrics.description: Day index on which simulated adoption reaches its maximum.

metrics.name: StabilityLastWindow
metrics.description: Average absolute day-over-day change in adoption over the last N days; lower indicates convergence.

validation_criteria.name: RMSE_threshold
validation_criteria.description: Calibration accepted if RMSE <= 0.05 over the calibration period.

validation_criteria.name: FinalAdoption_tolerance
validation_criteria.description: Absolute difference between simulated and observed final-day adoption <= 0.02.

validation_criteria.name: Convergence_rule
validation_criteria.description: Mean absolute change in adoption over last 7 days <= 0.005.

key_patterns.name: Heterogeneous baseline risk perception
key_patterns.description: Agents exhibit diverse risk_perception values in [0,1], likely non-uniform and segmentable by age_group and occupation.
key_patterns.relevance: Maps to heterogeneous initial mask propensity and differential sensitivity to social influence; informs priors and stratified calibration.

key_patterns.name: Multiplex network structure
key_patterns.description: Three layers (family, work_school, community) with different tie densities and strengths; edges may be directed and overlapping across layers.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific influence strengths and contact frequencies should be calibrated; directionality influences exposure asymmetry.

key_patterns.name: Clustered households and meso-scale work/school clusters
key_patterns.description: Family ties form small, dense cliques; work/school ties form medium-size clusters; community ties provide sparse bridging.
key_patterns.relevance: Expect faster local convergence within families, medium diffusion in work/school, and broader reach via community; guides weight and transmission parameters.

key_patterns.name: Early adoption driven by information exposure
key_patterns.description: train_data.csv includes received_info; adoption likely follows information receipt with a lag.
key_patterns.relevance: Estimate info-to-adoption hazard; separate exogenous information effects from peer influence to reduce confounding in calibration.

key_patterns.name: Potential homophily by age and occupation
key_patterns.description: Higher tie probability among agents sharing age_group or occupation; similar traits cluster in the network.
key_patterns.relevance: Adjust peer influence by similarity; homophily affects diffusion speed and critical thresholds.

key_patterns.name: Non-reciprocal edges in raw data
key_patterns.description: Adjacency lists may not be reciprocal; directedness can bias influence counts.
key_patterns.relevance: Requires symmetrization or explicit modeling of directed influence to avoid under/over-estimation of exposure.

key_patterns.name: Temporal convergence in late period
key_patterns.description: Adoption rates may stabilize toward the end of the calibration window (assess via decreasing day-over-day changes).
key_patterns.relevance: Use StabilityLastWindow to check convergence; helps tune persistence/decay parameters.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk_perception associated with higher initial and subsequent mask adoption probability.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via logistic regression; report odds ratio per unit increase in risk_perception.

key_relationships.relationship: Information receipt increases next-day adoption probability.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate discrete-time hazard difference or average treatment effect; expect medium to strong.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive peer effect from neighbors’ mask adoption, aggregated with layer weights.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate logistic slope lambda; strength varies by layer; family strongest.

key_relationships.relationship: Age segment differences in adoption propensity and responsiveness.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate group fixed effects; expect moderate heterogeneity.

key_relationships.relationship: Occupation influences contact structure and adoption (e.g., school mandates).
key_relationships.strength: Estimate group effects and interaction with work_school layer exposure.

symmetrize_edges.source: Multiplex network JSON (edges may be non-reciprocal)
symmetrize_edges.notes: Use undirected edges by default; keep optional directed mode for sensitivity.

layer_weights.source: Multiplex network JSON degree/clustering contrasts and typical contact intensity
layer_weights.notes: Calibrate via grid/CMA-ES against RMSE; constrain to sum to 1.

contact_rate_per_day.notes: Alternative: normalize to 1 using layer_weights if modeling influence by fractions rather than counts.

self_loops_removed.notes: Drop any self-references in adjacency lists.

value.form: logit(P0_i) = alpha0 + alpha_risk * risk_perception_i + alpha_age[age_group_i] + alpha_occ[occupation_i]

initial_mask_prob_model.source: agents CSV (risk_perception, age_group, occupation) + day 0/early days in train_data.csv
initial_mask_prob_model.notes: Fit coefficients via logistic regression on earliest days with variation; replace priors above after estimation.

risk_perception_distribution.notes: Use as prior for agents missing risk_perception or for synthetic agents.

info_transmission_prob.notes: Estimate by regressing received_info_t on neighbors’ received_info_{t-1} per layer.

exogenous_broadcast_rate.source: train_data.csv received_info not explained by neighbors

peer_effect_strength_lambda.source: Calibration to adoption response vs neighbor adoption share
peer_effect_strength_lambda.notes: In logistic: logit(p_adopt) += lambda * I_i,t where I is weighted neighbor fraction.

conformity_threshold_theta.source: Threshold model fit to adoption curves
conformity_threshold_theta.notes: If using threshold rule: adopt when I_i,t >= theta (with noise).

homophily_multiplier.notes: Multiply influence weight when attributes match; calibrate via segment-specific fit.

adoption_rule.value: P(wear_t=1 | wear_{t-1}=0) = 1 - exp(-lambda_peer * I_i,t - beta_info * received_info_{t-1} - beta0)
adoption_rule.notes: beta_info estimated from info→adoption hazard; beta0 is baseline adoption rate.

persistence_phi.notes: Can be conditioned on exposure to model habit reinforcement.

dropout_base_delta.source: P(wear_t=0 | wear_{t-1}=1, low exposure) from train_data.csv
dropout_base_delta.notes: Allow exposure-dependent dropout: delta_t = delta0 * (1 - I_i,t).

target_adoption_threshold.notes: Adjust per policy goals; compute first day simulated adoption >= threshold.

stability_window_N.notes: Average absolute day-over-day change over last 7 days.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Use a two-stage hybrid method: (1) Estimate micro-transition parameters from data via GLMs/survival models: initial propensity (alpha parameters), info→adoption effect (beta_info), persistence/dropout (phi, delta), and preliminary peer effect (lambda) using layer-weighted neighbor exposure. (2) Refine network-layer parameters and interaction strengths with simulation-based optimization (e.g., CMA-ES or Bayesian optimization) to minimize RMSE and MAE between simulated and observed daily adoption rates; include penalties for mismatch in PeakAdoptionDay, FinalAdoptionRate, and StabilityLastWindow. Apply stratified fits by age_group/occupation if segment residuals are systematic.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Evaluate on held-out days and subgroups. Compute RMSE and MAE on daily adoption rates; report FinalAdoptionRate, PeakAdoptionDay, TimeToTargetAdoption (with threshold from parameters), and StabilityLastWindow (N=7). Perform posterior predictive checks: distribution of time-to-adoption, segment-specific adoption curves, and sensitivity to symmetrization. Use bootstrapping over agents to quantify uncertainty and provide confidence intervals.

file_summaries:
- Overall structure/type: Tabular CSV; each row represents a single agent. No nested structures.
- Primary key: agent_id (integer) — unique identifier for each agent; use as node ID in the social network and to join with other datasets (e.g., edges).
- Attributes:
  - age_group (categorical: e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age) — demographic segment that can inform homophily, contact patterns, and differential influence rules.
  - occupation (categorical: e.g., Student, White Collar, Blue Collar) — role for assigning agents to interaction layers (school, workplace) and contact rates.
  - risk_perception (float in [0,1]) — baseline perceived risk; suitable as initial mask-wearing propensity or as a parameter modulating susceptibility to social influence and responsiveness to external information.
- Relationships/nesting: None encoded in this file; no edges or households. Relationships are implied via attributes (e.g., same occupation → likely co-layer contacts) and should be constructed externally using agent_id.
- Use in simulation:
  - Instantiate agents with heterogeneous traits; agent_id indexes nodes.
  - Initialize behavior: map risk_perception to initial probability of mask-wearing (e.g., direct or via a logistic transform possibly conditioned on age_group/occupation).
  - Network construction: use age_group/occupation to form layers and homophilous ties; set contact frequencies and influence weights accordingly.
  - Dynamics: risk_perception can act as a stable trait or an updateable state influenced by neighbors and interventions; age/occupation can modulate thresholds, conformity, or exposure.
  - Analysis/interventions: segment outcomes and policies by age_group/occupation; target high-contact or low-perception segments.

- Overall data structure and type:
  - JSON object representing a multiplex (multi-layer) social network as adjacency lists.
  - Top-level is a dictionary keyed by agent IDs (strings), values are dictionaries of lists.

- Meaning of keys or columns:
  - Top-level keys ("0", "1", …): unique agent identifiers (convertible to integers).
  - Nested keys:
    - family: list of agent IDs connected via household/family ties.
    - work_school: list of agent IDs connected via workplace/school ties.
    - community: list of agent IDs connected via broader community ties.
  - List elements are neighbor agent IDs (integers) referencing other agents in the same file.

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - Each agent has up to three adjacency lists, one per social layer.
  - Edges are specified per agent; reciprocity is not guaranteed by the data (i.e., may be directed unless symmetrized during preprocessing).
  - Layers are disjoint categories but neighbors can overlap across layers (an agent can be connected to the same person in multiple layers).
  - No weights or timestamps are provided; this is purely topological structure.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Agents: create one agent per top-level key with ID and membership in three layer-specific networks.
  - Network construction: build three graphs (family, work/school, community) or a single multiplex graph with layer tags. Decide whether to:
    - Treat edges as directed (as given) or
    - Symmetrize to undirected by adding reverse links.
  - Interaction dynamics:
    - Use layer-specific contact frequencies/weights (e.g., family > work/school > community) to modulate influence of mask adoption.
    - At each step, an agent samples neighbors from each layer according to layer weights to compute social influence toward adoption/abandonment.
    - Support heterogeneous exposure by aggregating influences across layers (e.g., weighted sum or threshold rules).
  - Initialization and validation:
    - Ensure all referenced IDs exist; handle any missing nodes or duplicates.
    - Optionally compute degrees per layer to set behavior parameters (e.g., higher conformity in dense family clusters).
  - Extensions:
    - Allow cross-layer spillover effects, targeted interventions on specific layers (e.g., workplace mandates), and time-varying edge activation probabilities per layer.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv:

- Data structure and type
  - CSV, long-format panel (time-series) data.
  - One record per agent per day; discrete-time steps.

- Columns and meanings
  - day: integer time index (non-negative), simulation timestep.
  - agent_id: integer unique identifier for an agent.
  - wearing_mask: boolean state indicating if the agent is currently wearing a mask.
  - received_info: boolean state indicating if the agent has received information/prompts about mask-wearing (e.g., via social contact or broadcast).

- Relationships or nested elements
  - No nesting; flat table.
  - Composite key (day, agent_id) identifies a unique state observation.
  - Temporal relationship: records for the same agent across increasing day values form a trajectory.
  - Potential causal/temporal dependency: wearing_mask at day t may depend on received_info and neighbors’ states at t-1 (network not included in this file).

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Agent initialization: use day 0 rows to set initial states for each agent (in sample, all agents start with wearing_mask=false and received_info=false).
  - State variables per agent: maintain booleans for wearing_mask and received_info; update each timestep.
  - Transition modeling/calibration: if multiple days exist in the full file, use it to estimate parameters (e.g., probability of adopting a mask after receiving info, persistence/decay, lag effects).
  - Validation/fitness: compare simulated trajectories to observed rows per (day, agent_id) to tune diffusion and compliance parameters.
  - Network dependency: social ties are not present here; must be provided/assumed elsewhere. received_info can be driven by network contagion or exogenous broadcasts; wearing_mask can depend on received_info and social influence.
  - Data handling: cast booleans correctly, treat day as discrete timestep, ensure full coverage or handle missing agent-days.

model_plan.description: Agent-based, multiplex-network diffusion model of mask-wearing that integrates peer influence, information propagation, and policy/venue enforcement. Calibrated on days 0-29, predicts days 30-39.

modules.name: NetworkPreprocessor
modules.description: Loads and prepares multiplex network: validates nodes, symmetrizes edges (optional), removes self-loops, computes degrees by layer, builds neighbor index structures.

notes: Runs effectively only at t=0; subsequent ticks keep structures static.
If directed_mode=true, skip symmetrization and preserve edge direction in exposure calculations.

modules.calibration_notes: Structural module; no direct stochastic parameters tied to observables.

modules.name: ExposureCalculator
modules.description: Computes layer-weighted social exposure I_i,t to mask-wearing from neighbors, adjusted by homophily and contact weights.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each agent i:
  for each layer L in {family, work, community}:
    N_iL = neighbor_index[i][L]
    if |N_iL| == 0: frac_L = 0
    else:
      w_sum = 0; masked_w_sum = 0
      for j in N_iL:
        w = 1.0
        if same_age(i,j): w *= params.homophily_weight_same_age
        if same_occ(i,j): w *= params.homophily_weight_same_occ
        w_sum += w
        masked_w_sum += w * adoption_state[j,t-1]
      frac_L = masked_w_sum / max(w_sum, eps)
    I_i += params.layer_weight_L * frac_L
  # smooth exposure
  signal.exposure_I[i,t] = (1 - params.exposure_smoothing_gamma) * I_i + params.exposure_smoothing_gamma * signal.exposure_I[i,t-1]
notes: Smoothing provides stability in highly clustered structures.

modules.calibration_notes: Calibrate layer weights and homophily multipliers indirectly via AdoptionDynamics RMSE.

modules.name: PolicyAuthority
modules.description: Schedules and emits daily policy signals: mandate level, enforcement, communication, subsidy; allows ramping after start_day.

update_rule.pseudocode:
if t < params.policy_start_day or t > params.policy_end_day:
  mandate = 0.0; comm = 0.0; enforce = 0.0; subsidy = 0.0
else:
  ramp = min(1.0, params.policy_ramp_rate * (t - params.policy_start_day))
  mandate = params.mandate_level_base * ramp
  comm = params.communication_intensity_base * ramp
  enforce = min(1.0, params.enforcement_level_global * (1 + params.mandate_to_enforcement_multiplier * mandate))
  subsidy = params.subsidy_incentive_base * ramp
emit signals
notes: Ramping smooths sudden jumps at policy start.
Enforcement can scale with mandate intensity.

modules.calibration_notes: Policy schedule is externally specified; magnitude parameters can be tuned indirectly.

modules.name: InfoDiffusion
modules.description: Generates received_info per agent via neighbor info contagion and exogenous broadcasts influenced by policy communication.

notes: Combines broadcast and neighbor contagion without double counting via independence approximation.
Memory decay prevents perpetual info saturation.

modules.calibration_notes: Tune info_transmission_* and exogenous_broadcast_rate against daily received_info rate (train_data).

modules.name: AttendanceAndContacts
modules.description: Allocates daily contact opportunities across layers; provides effective contact weights for influence and enforcement.

notes: Outputs daily weights that can modulate exposure or enforcement effects.
Policy closures can be modeled by reducing corresponding open fractions (not shown here but allowed).

modules.calibration_notes: Fractions can be tuned indirectly; defaults reflect provided parameters.

modules.name: LocationEnforcement
modules.description: Applies location-specific mask requirements and enforcement, influencing effective adoption at locations.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for L in {family, work, community}:
  req = params.location_mask_requirement_level[L]
  eff = params.location_enforcement_level[L] * signal.policy.enforcement_level[t] * req
  signal.location_effective_enforcement[t][L] = min(1.0, eff)
# optional reporting noise (not used in dynamics)
observed = clip(signal.location_effective_enforcement[t] + Normal(0, params.location_report_noise_sigma), 0, 1)
notes: Families typically have low formal enforcement; public/work can be higher.
This signal feeds AdoptionDynamics via policy_effect_strength.

modules.calibration_notes: Not directly observed; effect tuned via adoption fit.

modules.name: AdoptionDynamics
modules.description: Updates mask-wearing state using discrete-time hazard with peer exposure, info, policy, risk perception, and habit persistence/dropout.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each agent i:
  # persistence/dropout
  if adoption_state[i,t-1] == 1:
    # persistence can be reinforced by exposure
    phi = min(1.0, params.phi_persist + 0.1 * signal.exposure_I[i,t])
    stay_masked = bernoulli(phi)
    if stay_masked:
      adoption_state[i,t] = 1
      continue
    else:
      # dropout; lower when exposure high
      delta = params.delta_drop * (1 - signal.exposure_I[i,t])
      dropout = bernoulli(delta)
      adoption_state[i,t] = 0 if dropout else 1
      continue
  # adoption for previously unmasked
  I = min(params.peer_influence_cap, signal.exposure_I[i,t])
  info = state.person.received_info[i,t-1]
  policy_effect = params.policy_effect_strength * (
      signal.policy.mandate_level[t] +
      0.5 * (signal.location_effective_enforcement[t].family + signal.location_effective_enforcement[t].work + signal.location_effective_enforcement[t].community)
  )
  # individual propensity
  base = params.beta0 + params.lambda_peer * I + params.beta_info * info + policy_effect - params.mask_disutility + 0.8 * risk_perception[i]
  # thresholded logistic
  z = base - params.adoption_threshold
  p_adopt = 1 / (1 + exp(-z))
  adoption_state[i,t] = bernoulli(p_adopt)
  # update risk perception decay
  risk_perception[i] = max(0, risk_perception[i] * (1 - params.risk_perception_decay))
notes: Risk perception enters additively; decays slowly over time.
peer_influence_cap avoids unrealistically high I due to dense clusters.

modules.calibration_notes: Fit lambda_peer, beta_info, beta0, phi_persist, delta_drop, mask_disutility, adoption_threshold, policy_effect_strength using daily adoption rate RMSE and additional constraints.

modules.name: Aggregation
modules.description: Computes population-level observables from agent states for calibration and evaluation.

update_rule.pseudocode:
adoption_rate = mean_i(adoption_state[i,t])
received_info_rate = mean_i(received_info[i,t])
emit observable.adoption_rate_daily[t] = adoption_rate
emit observable.received_info_rate_daily[t] = received_info_rate
notes: Outputs are used by metrics; no parameters.

modules.calibration_notes: Derived from states; no direct calibration.

verification_results.summary: The simulation code is syntactically correct, imports are appropriate, and it implements a reasonable agent-based model with social influence, information diffusion, and policy effects. It loads data if available, synthesizes otherwise, runs for 60 days, flags the prediction window (days 30–39), and evaluates metrics (including RMSE over days 0–29). Error handling is acceptable, and a direct main() call is present. There are several minor issues: a metric naming/definition mismatch (FinalAdoptionRate), potential data schema mismatch (age vs age_group), exposure smoothing convention, unused noisy enforcement, and calibration grid not using the provided search bounds/parameter names. Performance could be heavy if calibration is enabled with large N, but defaults keep calibration off.

issues.description: FinalAdoptionRate metric is implemented as the absolute error between simulated and observed final-day adoption, not the simulated final-day adoption rate itself as described. This is a naming/definition mismatch.
issues.solution: Either rename the metric to FinalAdoptionRateError or change the implementation to report the simulated adoption rate on the final calibration day and add a separate metric for the absolute difference if needed.

issues.description: Person and Location classes define attributes but their behaviors are not implemented (methods are pass) and are not used in the simulation. The simulation uses vectorized modules instead.
issues.solution: Either implement or remove unused behaviors. If keeping the vectorized approach, clarify via comments that these classes are placeholders for schema documentation and not used in the run.

issues.description: Calibration grid ignores the specification's search_bounds and parameter naming (e.g., uses 'lambda_peer' instead of 'peer_influence_strength') and does not honor 'information_campaign_intensity' from the task.
issues.solution: Map spec parameter names to internal ones (e.g., peer_influence_strength -> lambda_peer) and, if provided, read and apply search_bounds from config/task. Optionally include information_campaign_intensity in PolicyAuthority or InfoDiffusion.

issues.description: Data schema mismatch: loader expects 'age_group' while the task mentions 'age'. This can lead to missing homophily signals if datasets contain 'age' instead of 'age_group'.
issues.solution: Support both 'age' and 'age_group' (derive age_group bins from age if only age is provided). Update expected columns and maps accordingly.

issues.description: Exposure smoothing applies exposure_smoothed = (1 - gamma)*exposure + gamma*exposure_prev. Typically, smoothing uses gamma to weight current signal (gamma*current + (1-gamma)*previous).
issues.solution: Consider switching to exposure_smoothed = gamma * exposure + (1 - gamma) * exposure_prev, or document the intended meaning of gamma.

issues.description: Observed enforcement with noise is computed but unused, so the noise has no effect on dynamics or outputs.
issues.solution: Use the noisy enforcement in adoption dynamics if the model intends to incorporate perception noise, or remove the noise call to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The model flags the prediction window but only saves aggregate rates. The task emphasizes predicting agents' mask-wearing behavior for days 30–39; per-agent outputs are not saved.
issues.solution: Optionally add a function to save per-agent adoption_state for days 30–39 (e.g., a long-form CSV with columns day, agent_id, wearing_mask).

issues.description: When 'agent_id' is missing in agent_attributes.csv, load_agents() continues without creating it, leading to a KeyError later and returning None. The message is generic.
issues.solution: Explicitly check for 'agent_id'. If missing, raise a clear error or synthesize sequential IDs, ensuring alignment with network keys.

issues.description: Calibration runs full simulations for each grid combination with population_size defaulting to 10000, which can be slow.
issues.solution: For calibration, reduce population_size, T, or network degree; or add early stopping/parallelization. Default to a smaller N when calibration_enabled is true.

issues.description: Attendance/contact weights are not influenced by policy or time-varying openings beyond static config. This limits fidelity of location-based dynamics.
issues.solution: Adjust weights based on policy_signals (e.g., modify open fractions after policy_start_day) to reflect closures/reopenings.

feedback.summary: The simulation is structurally sound and runs end-to-end with synthesized data, but several issues prevent strict adherence to the task and hinder evaluation accuracy. The most critical problems are a metric-definition mismatch (FinalAdoptionRate), missing JSON outputs for the evaluation pipeline, schema fragility (age vs age_group, agent_id handling), and misalignment between calibration parameters and the task specification. Addressing these, along with minor logic fixes (exposure smoothing convention, unused enforcement noise), will improve correctness, evaluability, and alignment with real-world data.

def load_agents(self) -> Optional[pd.DataFrame]:
    try:
        df = pd.read_csv(self.agent_file)
        # Ensure agent_id exists or synthesize
        if "agent_id" not in df.columns:
            print("Warning: agent_id missing; synthesizing sequential IDs.")
            df.insert(0, "agent_id", np.arange(len(df), dtype=int))
        df["agent_id"] = df["agent_id"].astype(int)
        # Risk perception default
        if "risk_perception" not in df.columns:
            df["risk_perception"] = 0.5
        df["risk_perception"] = df["risk_perception"].clip(0, 1).astype(float)
        # Occupation default
        if "occupation" not in df.columns:
            df["occupation"] = "Unknown"
        # Age/age_group handling
        if "age_group" not in df.columns:
            if "age" in df.columns:
                bins = [0, 18, 35, 55, 200]
                labels = ["Youth", "Young Adult", "Middle Age", "Older Adult"]
                df["age_group"] = pd.cut(df["age"].astype(float), bins=bins, labels=labels, right=False).astype(str)
            else:
                df["age_group"] = "Unknown"
        # Optional heterogeneity defaults
        for col, default_val in [
            ("compliance_probability", 0.5),
            ("policy_sensitivity", 1.0),
            ("susceptibility_to_influence", 1.0),
            ("peer_influence_weight", 1.0),
        ]:
            if col not in df.columns:
                df[col] = default_val
        self.agents_df = df
        return df
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Could not load agents file at {self.agent_file}: {e}")
        self.agents_df = None
        return None

    def linspace_bound(key, default, n, low=None, high=None):
        lo, hi = bounds.get(key, [low if low is not None else default, high if high is not None else default])

def save_json_results(self, filename: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    sim_adoption = list(map(float, self.observables["adoption_rate"]))
    s, e = self.prediction_window
    pred_slice = sim_adoption[s:e+1] if (s is not None and e is not None) else []
    metrics = self.evaluate()
    out = {
        "metadata": {
            "simulation_days": int(self.T),
            "population_size": int(self.N),
            "random_seed": int(self.config.get("random_seed", 42))
        },
        "prediction_window": {"start_day": int(s), "end_day": int(e)},
        "daily_adoption": sim_adoption,
        "prediction_window_adoption": pred_slice,
        "metrics": {k: (None if (isinstance(v, float) and (np.isnan(v) or np.isinf(v))) else v) for k, v in metrics.items()},
    }
    if filename:
        with open(filename, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(out, f, ensure_ascii=False)
    return out

def main() -> None:
    config = {
        "simulation_days": 60,
        "random_seed": 42,
        "calibration_enabled": False,
    }
    if config.get("calibration_enabled", False):
        print("Starting calibration...")
        best_config = Simulation.calibrate_grid(config)
        print("Using calibrated configuration.")
        sim = Simulation(config=best_config)
    else:
        sim = Simulation(config=config)
    sim.run()
    metrics = sim.evaluate()
    print("Evaluation metrics:")
    for k, v in metrics.items():
        print(f"  {k}: {v}")
    # Export JSON for external evaluators
    sim.save_json_results("results.json")
    sim.visualize()
    sim.save_results("results.csv")
    sim.save_prediction_results("prediction_window_results.csv", per_agent_filename="prediction_window_per_agent.csv")

# Execute main for both direct execution and sandbox wrapper invocation
main()
